title: Steel conduit systems
summary: Covers steel conduit systems: advantages and disadvantages, galvanised and black enamelled finishes, sizes, fixings and the specialist tools used.

sections.heading: Advantages and disadvantages
paragraphs: Steel conduit protects the conductors well and allows easy rewiring, but it costs more than some systems and can suffer from moisture and corrosion.
bullets: Advantages: good mechanical protection to conductors; easy rewiring; minimises fire risks; can be used as the circuit protective conductor
Disadvantages: under certain conditions moisture is liable to form inside; expensive compared with some other systems; liable to corrosion when subject to acid, alkali and other fumes

sections.heading: Finishes and sizes
paragraphs: Galvanised conduit is used outdoors or where steam or dampness is present. Black enamelled conduit is for general work in dry situations.
bullets: Black enamelled: general work in dry situations

sections.heading: Fixings, accessories and tools
paragraphs: There are different methods of fixing conduit to a surface. Many accessories are used when installing conduit, and some are for inspection purposes.
Specialist steel conduit tools include a bending machine, formers, and stocks and dies.
bullets: Saddles with spacer bars and distance pieces are common on surface mountings
A crampet can be used when conduit is sunk into a wall
Specialist tools: bending machine, formers, stocks and dies
